name: Long runs of consecutive integers with distinct totients (up to 10^12)
description: construct() -> {'start': s, 'length': k} with s >= 1, 1 <= k <= 200 and s + k - 1 <= 10^12. The values phi(s), ..., phi(s + k - 1) must be pairwise distinct (exact factorization). Maximize k. Long runs below 10^12 are finite evidence; (log 10^12)^c is about 27.6^c.

sources.locator: Paul Erdős, Carl Pomerance and András Sárközy, On Locally Repeated Values of Certain Arithmetic Functions. III (1987). Crossref record inspected; Erdős Problem #1004 page inspected (does some n <= x have phi(n+1), ..., phi(n+K) distinct for K = (log x)^c? Erdős, Pomerance and Sárközy proved K <= n/exp(c(log n)^(1/3))). No finite values are documented. Long runs below 10^12 are finite evidence; (log 10^12)^c is about 27.6^c.
Erdős Problem #1004 (open); statement, history and current bounds reviewed 2026-09-24.
JSP-000836; pinned discovery source, independently paraphrased. Primary mathematical attribution follows the papers above.
